answers.goal: show that municipal audits shape city politics more than elections do

draftText: Robert Moses, who ran New York's parks department for twenty-six years, once said that "those who can, build; those who can't, criticize." The city's own audit that year found that 63% of capital projects overran their budgets. Municipal audits, unlike elections, are conducted continuously, and it is this constancy that gives them their power. The 1975 fiscal crisis nearly bankrupted the city and handed budget authority to an unelected control board.

existingSources: World Health Organization, Global Report on Sleep and Shift Work (2024)
draftText: According to the 2024 WHO report on shift work, night workers lose an average of 11 days of sleep per year. Matthew Walker has written that sleep loss of this scale measurably shortens lifespan. The report also states that 40% of nurses in the surveyed hospitals met the criteria for chronic sleep deprivation.

answers.goal: a Sheffield family across the 1984 miners' strike
answers.successSignal: an agent asks for the full manuscript

draftText: Annie Bewick set down her tea and said, "They'll not break us before Christmas." Her brother had been at Orgreave in June, where mounted police charged the picket line, and he had not spoken of it since. The Cutlery Works on Arundel Street had laid off ninety men that spring. Annie thought the strike would end the way her mother's had, in silence and a smaller house.

answers.goal: argue that mandated reading lists dull comprehension

draftText: I think the reading list is a kind of scaffolding that we forgot to take down. Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, and a curriculum can freeze just as hard. My argument is simple: what a child is required to read, they learn to resent. This is the part of the essay where I expect disagreement.
